chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd al-Karim al-Kazzaz, from Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-Awar, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), said: Every supplication is veiled from the heaven until one sends blessings upon Muhammad and his family.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a supplication to reach heaven according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes sending blessings (salawat) as a spiritual prerequisite that lifts the veil from supplications, ensuring their acceptance in the heavenly realm. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *wasilah* (means of approach), where the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt serve as the intercessory channel through which divine grace flows to the supplicant.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3.  Amirul Momineen (a.s.) said,  “No supplication reaches the  heaven  unless  one  recites  salutation  on  Muhammad (s.a.w.s.) and his progeny.”
